identification.summary: TA4922 is Proofpoint's designation for a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking cybercrime cluster that aims to obtain remote access to victim environments for fraud, data theft and resale of access [S1][S3]. Proofpoint says it runs more distinct campaigns than any other cybercrime actor it tracks [S1][S2]. Lures are localized HR, payroll, tax and invoice themes, and the actor tries to move victims from email to messaging platforms such as LINE, WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams [S3]. Its malware set includes Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, ValleyRAT (Winos4.0) and, from May 2026, PackClient [S1][S3][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Proofpoint says it has tracked malicious email campaigns associated with TA4922 since spring 2025 [S3][S6].
identification.notes: Proofpoint states the activity does not overlap one to one with Silver Fox / Void Arachne and tracks TA4922 as a distinct cluster; it judges campaigns align with cybercrime rather than espionage objectives, while other researchers link Silver Fox to espionage [S4]. A Risky Business item lists TA4922 as a Silver Fox alias, so cross-vendor naming is not settled [S4]. No MITRE ATT&CK group ID or Microsoft name is recorded in this encyclopedia.

attribution.confidence: Proofpoint describes the actor as 'suspected' Chinese and Chinese-speaking, likely financially motivated [S1][S3]. No government attribution located.
attribution.basis: Proofpoint email telemetry and malware analysis as reported by secondary coverage [S1][S2][S3]. Proofpoint assessed with high confidence that the actor is likely using LLMs to develop its Python malware, based on an unchanged placeholder key and similar artifacts left in code [S2]; BleepingComputer-derived coverage phrased this more tentatively [S4].

objectives: Financial gain through remote access to victim systems, used for fraud, data theft and resale of access [S1][S3]. Proofpoint notes surveillance features (keylogging, screen and webcam capture) could be sold to or used by espionage actors [S1][S5].

regions: Japan (most frequent, first Atlas RAT campaign March 2026) [S3][S6]
United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, South Africa (expansion in 2026) [S1][S3]
China (May 2026 tax lures) and India (July 2026 Hindi tax lures) with PackClient [S5]
targeting.notes: Targeting is by language and locale of lure rather than reported industry; Proofpoint's PackClient reporting did not state victim counts or industries [S5]. Sources differ on the exact historical country list [S6].

capabilities.summary: Localized phishing impersonating HR departments and tax authorities, with short initial emails asking victims to move to LINE, WhatsApp or Teams [S3]. Delivery uses ZIP archives (some hosted on GoFile) with DLL sideloading [S6]. Atlas RAT (AtlasCross) provides reconnaissance, file exfiltration, keylogging, screen/audio/video capture and further payload download [S4]. RomulusLoader is a C-based loader first seen late March 2026 that stages RMM tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture [S6]. SilentRunLoader is a Python loader/stealer targeting browser credentials, likely LLM-assisted [S2][S4][S6]. ValleyRAT (Winos4.0) variants are also used [S1][S4]. PackClient, a modular C2 framework sold on Telegram, was delivered via a ZIP-borne executable in China and via ISO plus DLL sideload and Donut Loader in India [S5].

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking, financially motivated cluster tracked by Proofpoint; relationship to Silver Fox / Void Arachne unresolved [S3][S4].
diamond.capability: Localized phishing, social-engineering pivot to messaging apps, DLL sideloading, custom loaders, Atlas RAT, ValleyRAT, PackClient, LLM-assisted Python malware [S2][S3][S5][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: ZIP archives hosted on file-sharing services such as GoFile and RMM tooling such as AnyDesk used post-compromise [S6]; IOCs are in the Proofpoint post, which was not opened [S3].
diamond.victim: Organizations in Japan and East Asia, expanding to UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa, and India [S1][S3][S5][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: Cybercrime ecosystem with possible monetization through resale of access; surveillance features could serve espionage buyers [S1][S5].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints reached through email attachments and links, plus messaging platforms (LINE, WhatsApp, Teams) used for out-of-band social engineering [S3].

gaps: Proofpoint primary posts (TA4922 going global; Carry-On Compromise PackClient) could not be opened (host unreachable); content relies on secondary coverage and search summaries [S1][S3][S5].
Victim sectors, counts and IOCs are not captured.
Relationship to Silver Fox / Void Arachne is disputed across sources [S4]; do not merge facts without primary text.
No government attribution, MITRE ID or Microsoft name located.
Details of 2025 activity (spring 2025 onward) are not public in gathered sources.
A flagged third-party claim of weaponized VPN installers is unconfirmed and excluded.
Fortian reported a TA4922-attributed campaign against Australian organizations on LinkedIn; not independently verified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Personnel email and personal messaging apps (LINE, WhatsApp, Teams) are the relevant terrain; the threat is to contractor and partner-nation staff more than to military networks directly [S3]. STEP 2: Localized lures and rapid campaign tempo favor defenders who tailor awareness by country and language [S1][S3]. STEP 3: Template is HR or tax lure, ZIP or ISO with DLL sideload, loader, RAT or RMM tool, then data theft and access resale [S3][S5][S6]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued fraud-oriented intrusions of commercial organizations in Indo-Pacific and Europe. MDCOA is resale of access or surveillance tooling to an espionage actor against allied government or defense-industry staff [S1][S5]. Candidate indicators: unexpected AnyDesk/SyncFuture installs, DLL sideloading from user-writable paths, archives from GoFile, and requests to move conversations to LINE/WhatsApp [S3][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Proofpoint reporting and share locale-specific lure themes with Indo-Pacific partners [S3]. (2) Authorities: activity is criminal, so response for non-DoD victims runs through law enforcement and CISA channels rather than military authorities. (3) Mission assurance: restrict RMM tools and sideloading on DoD-adjacent contractor endpoints, and treat personal messaging pivots as a reportable event [S3][S6]. (4) Coordination: DC3/DIB CS program and allied CERTs in Japan, Taiwan and India; reassess if access resale to espionage actors is observed [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: TA4922 is a Chinese-speaking cybercrime cluster that employs localized HR, payroll, tax, and invoice lures to deliver various malware families, including Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, and SilentRunLoader. The actor conducts targeted email campaigns, often impersonating trusted authorities, to facilitate credential phishing and fraud. TA4922's operational tempo is high, with a focus on obtaining remote access for financial gain, and it has shown a rapid evolution in its malware arsenal. The group is also noted for using social engineering to shift communications from email to messaging platforms, enhancing their phishing efforts.
